## Proof

**Answer: Yes.** Such an $F$-measurable $g:\Omega\to X$ with $g=f$ $P'$-a.e. always exists. (The nonatomic hypothesis is not needed; the result holds for every probability space.)

We use two standard lemmas and then combine them.

---

**Lemma 1 (real-valued versioning).** *Let $u:\Omega\to\mathbb{R}$ be $F'$-measurable. There exists an $F$-measurable $v:\Omega\to\mathbb{R}$ with $v=u$ $P'$-a.e.*

*Proof of Lemma 1.* Recall that the completion has the form
$$F'=\{B\cup N:\; B\in F,\; N\subseteq M\text{ for some }M\in F\text{ with }P(M)=0\},\qquad P'(B\cup N)=P(B).$$

*Indicators.* Let $u=\mathbf 1_A$ with $A=B\cup N\in F'$, $B\in F$, $N\subseteq M$, $P(M)=0$. Set $v=\mathbf 1_B$. On $M^{c}$ we have $N\cap M^{c}=\varnothing$, hence $A\cap M^{c}=B\cap M^{c}$ and so $\mathbf 1_A=\mathbf 1_B$ on $M^{c}$. Thus $\{u\neq v\}\subseteq M$ and $P'(\{u\neq v\})\le P'(M)=P(M)=0$.

*Simple functions.* If $u=\sum_{i=1}^{k}a_i\mathbf 1_{A_i}$, apply the indicator case to each $A_i$ to get $B_i\in F$ with $\mathbf 1_{A_i}=\mathbf 1_{B_i}$ a.e.; set $v=\sum a_i\mathbf 1_{B_i}$. Then $v$ is $F$-measurable and $u=v$ off the finite union of the corresponding null sets, hence a.e.

*Non-negative functions.* Let $u\ge 0$ be $F'$-measurable. Choose $F'$-simple $s_n\uparrow u$. By the simple case, for each $n$ pick an $F$-simple $t_n$ with $t_n=s_n$ $P'$-a.e.; let $N=\bigcup_n\{t_n\neq s_n\}$, so $P'(N)=0$. Define
$$v(\omega)=\begin{cases}\lim_{n\to\infty}t_n(\omega),& \omega\in N^{c}\text{ (where the limit exists and equals }u(\omega)\text{)},\\ 0,&\omega\in N.\end{cases}$$
More precisely set $v=\limsup_{n}t_n$; this is $F$-measurable, and on $N^{c}$ we have $t_n=s_n\uparrow u$, so $\lim t_n=u$. Hence $v=u$ on $N^{c}$, i.e. $P'$-a.e.

*General case.* Write $u=u^{+}-u^{-}$ and apply the non-negative case to each part. ∎

---

**Lemma 2 (Hilbert-cube embedding).** *Every compact metric space $X$ admits a homeomorphic embedding $\varphi:X\hookrightarrow H:=[0,1]^{\mathbb N}$ into the Hilbert cube. Its image $\varphi(X)$ is compact, hence closed (in particular Borel) in $H$.*

*Proof of Lemma 2.* Since $X$ is compact metric, $C(X)$ is separable; pick a countable dense $\{h_n\}_{n\ge1}\subseteq C(X)$ with $0\le h_n\le 1$ (rescale a countable dense subset of $C(X)$). The map $\varphi(x)=(h_1(x),h_2(x),\dots)$ is continuous $X\to H$. It is injective because $\{h_n\}$ separates points (density in $C(X)$), and a continuous injection from a compact space to a Hausdorff space is a homeomorphism onto its image. The image of a compact space is compact, and compact subsets of the Hausdorff space $H$ are closed. ∎

---

**Main proof.** Fix $\varphi:X\hookrightarrow H$ as in Lemma 2 and write $\pi_n:H\to[0,1]$ for the $n$-th coordinate. Set
$$u_n:=\pi_n\circ\varphi\circ f:\Omega\longrightarrow[0,1].$$
Each $u_n$ is $F'$-measurable (composition of Borel maps with the $F'$-measurable $f$). By Lemma 1, for each $n$ choose an $F$-measurable $v_n:\Omega\to[0,1]$ with $v_n=u_n$ $P'$-a.e. Let
$$N_n:=\{v_n\neq u_n\},\qquad P'(N_n)=0,\qquad N:=\bigcup_{n\ge1}N_n,\qquad P'(N)=0.$$

Define $h:\Omega\to H$ by $h(\omega)=(v_1(\omega),v_2(\omega),\dots)$. Since $H$ carries the product topology and $[0,1]$ is second countable, $\mathrm{Borel}(H)$ equals the product $\sigma$-algebra, generated by the coordinate projections; each $v_n$ is $F$-measurable, so $h$ is $F$-measurable.

On $N^{c}$ we have $v_n=u_n$ for every $n$, hence
$$h=\varphi\circ f\in\varphi(X)\quad\text{on }N^{c}.$$
Set $A:=h^{-1}(\varphi(X))=\{\omega:h(\omega)\in\varphi(X)\}$. Since $\varphi(X)$ is closed (Borel) in $H$ and $h$ is $F$-measurable, $A\in F$. Moreover $N^{c}\subseteq A$, so $P'(A^{c})\le P'(N)=0$; because $A^{c}\in F$, this gives $P(A^{c})=P'(A^{c})=0$.

Pick a base point $x_0\in X$ and define $g:\Omega\to X$ by
$$g(\omega)=\begin{cases}\varphi^{-1}(h(\omega)),& \omega\in A,\\ x_0,& \omega\in A^{c}.\end{cases}$$

*$g$ is $F$-measurable.* Let $B\subseteq X$ be Borel. Since $\varphi$ is a homeomorphism, $\varphi(B)$ is Borel in the subspace $\varphi(X)$; as $\varphi(X)$ is closed in $H$, there is a Borel set $C\subseteq H$ with $\varphi(B)=C\cap\varphi(X)$. Then
$$g^{-1}(B)=\bigl(A\cap h^{-1}(C)\bigr)\;\cup\;\bigl(A^{c}\cap\{x_0\in B\}\bigr).$$
Both $A\cap h^{-1}(C)$ and $A^{c}\cap\{x_0\in B\}$ belong to $F$, so $g^{-1}(B)\in F$.

*$g=f$ $P'$-a.e.* On $N^{c}\subseteq A$,
$$g=\varphi^{-1}\circ h=\varphi^{-1}\circ\varphi\circ f=f.$$
Since $P'(N)=0$, we have $g=f$ $P'$-a.e.

Thus the desired $F$-measurable $g:\Omega\to X$ exists. ∎

*Non-negative functions.* Let $u\ge 0$ be $F'$-measurable. Choose $F'$-simple $s_n\uparrow u$. By the simple case, for each $n$ pick an $F$-simple $t_n$ with $t_n=s_n$ $P'$-a.e.; let $N=\bigcup_n\{t_n\neq s_n\}$, so $P'(N)=0$. Define
$$v(\omega)=\begin{cases}\lim_{n\to\infty}t_n(\omega),& \omega\in N^{c}\text{ (where the limit exists and equals }u(\omega)\text{)},\\ 0,&\omega\in N.\end{cases}$$
More precisely set $v=\limsup_{n}t_n$; this is $F$-measurable, and on $N^{c}$ we have $t_n=s_n\uparrow u$, so $\lim t_n=u$. Hence $v=u$ on $N^{c}$, i.e. $P'$-a.e.

The map $\varphi(x)=(h_1(x),h_2(x),\dots)$ is continuous $X\to H$. $$u_n:=\pi_n\circ\varphi\circ f:\Omega\longrightarrow[0,1].$$
Each $u_n$ is $F'$-measurable (composition of Borel maps with the $F'$-measurable $f$). By Lemma 1, for each $n$ choose an $F$-measurable $v_n:\Omega\to[0,1]$ with $v_n=u_n$ $P'$-a.e. Let
$$N_n:=\{v_n\neq u_n\},\qquad P'(N_n)=0,\qquad N:=\bigcup_{n\ge1}N_n,\qquad P'(N)=0.$$

Define $h:\Omega\to H$ by $h(\omega)=(v_1(\omega),v_2(\omega),\dots)$. Since $H$ carries the product topology and $[0,1]$ is second countable, $\mathrm{Borel}(H)$ equals the product $\sigma$-algebra, generated by the coordinate projections; each $v_n$ is $F$-measurable, so $h$ is $F$-measurable.

On $N^{c}$ we have $v_n=u_n$ for every $n$, hence
$$h=\varphi\circ f\in\varphi(X)\quad\text{on }N^{c}.$$
Set $A:=h^{-1}(\varphi(X))=\{\omega:h(\omega)\in\varphi(X)\}$. Since $\varphi(X)$ is closed (Borel) in $H$ and $h$ is $F$-measurable, $A\in F$. Moreover $N^{c}\subseteq A$, so $P'(A^{c})\le P'(N)=0$; because $A^{c}\in F$, this gives $P(A^{c})=P'(A^{c})=0$.

Pick a base point $x_0\in X$ and define $g:\Omega\to X$ by
$$g(\omega)=\begin{cases}\varphi^{-1}(h(\omega)),& \omega\in A,\\ x_0,& \omega\in A^{c}.\end{cases}$$

*$g$ is $F$-measurable.* Let $B\subseteq X$ be Borel. Since $\varphi$ is a homeomorphism, $\varphi(B)$ is Borel in the subspace $\varphi(X)$; as $\varphi(X)$ is closed in $H$, there is a Borel set $C\subseteq H$ with $\varphi(B)=C\cap\varphi(X)$. Then
$$g^{-1}(B)=\bigl(A\cap h^{-1}(C)\bigr)\;\cup\;\bigl(A^{c}\cap\{x_0\in B\}\bigr).$$
Both $A\cap h^{-1}(C)$ and $A^{c}\cap\{x_0\in B\}$ belong to $F$, so $g^{-1}(B)\in F$.

*$g=f$ $P'$-a.e.* On $N^{c}\subseteq A$,
$$g=\varphi^{-1}\circ h=\varphi^{-1}\circ\varphi\circ f=f.$$
Since $P'(N)=0$, we have $g=f$ $P'$-a.e.

Thus the desired $F$-measurable $g:\Omega\to X$ exists. ∎
